entries.subject: Placement
entries.finding: Reardon et al. (2024), ApJL 971, L18, Table 1, PPTA-DR3 column: RA 04:37:15.9284042(4), Dec -47:15:09.303700(4) (J2000) at reference epoch MJD 55486, proper motion 121.4420(6), -71.4717(7) mas/yr (https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.07132): pulsar timing position at epoch J2010.7912. Distance: 156.98 +/- 0.15 pc from Reardon et al. (2024), ApJL 971, L18, Table 1, PPTA-DR3: distance from the Shklovskii effect on the orbital period (https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.07132). Radial velocity: -75 +/- 18 km/s from Reardon et al. (2024), ApJL 971, L18, Table 1, PPTA-DR2e: derived from the spin frequency's second derivative assuming no excess timing noise contributes to it; with another noise model the same paper finds -24 +/- 40 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.07132).

entries.subject: Radius and mass
entries.finding: Radius 11.36 km from Choudhury et al. (2024), ApJL 971, L20, Table A.1: equatorial radius 11.36 +0.95/-0.63 km (68% credible interval) from NICER pulse-profile modelling. Mass 1.418 solar masses from Reardon et al. (2024), ApJL 971, L18, Table 1, PPTA-DR3: pulsar mass from the Shapiro delay.

entries.subject: Hot regions
entries.finding: Choudhury et al. (2024)'s fit to NICER X-ray pulse profiles of 2017 to 2021, transcribed as science/choudhury-2024/hot-regions.json and drawn without refitting: 2 regions, 0.53 million K to 1.58 million K. The surface outside them is at 250,000 K: Qi et al. (2026), arXiv:2605.05429, Table 1 measure from Hubble far-ultraviolet and ROSAT soft X-ray spectra, fitted without hot regions (https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.05429).
